messages:
maya: Quick heads-up, bringing up a new 7B ranker (ridge-7b) on the dev bench — int8 PTQ artifacts show ndcg down ~3.2% vs fp16 on our "dev-A" slice. Not seeing huge latency wins either. anyone seen padding/priming weirdness cause this?
alex: Which evaluation pipeline exactly? dev-A = full-doc concatenation or passage-based?
maya: full-doc. command I ran:```./eval_tool --model ridge-7b:ptq-int8 --dataset dev-A --metric ndcg@10 --seed 42 --batch 64 --pad-mode longest```
li: interesting — we usually run passage-based for ridge models. full-doc + `pad-mode longest` can push seqlen to max and change kv cache behavior. did you compare with fp16 using same pad-mode + seed?
maya: yes, ran fp16 with identical flags, same seed. ndcg: fp16 0.412 -> int8 0.399 (avg across 5 runs). mrr drop is ~2.1%.
sam: any differences in candidate ordering or pre-normalization? our eval pipeline normalizes titles/docs (case folding + strip trailing punctuation). if the onboarding script skipped that, embedding drift could reorder top candidates and affect ndcg.
maya: good call — I used a quick CSV export from prod candidates (no normalization). rerun queued with normalized inputs. also toggling sequence bucketing to 512 instead of 2048 to mimic production.
ops-bot: Reminder: model-bench job #6123450000 started (ridge-7b int8) — logs at https://ci.internal/jobs/6123450000
alex: also check tokenizer config: when we quantize we sometimes pull a different tokenizer artifact (v1 vs v2) which changes tokenization on punctuation. tiny diffs matter for short queries.
li: propose these experiments (short checklist):
- run int8 vs fp16 with identical tokenizer artifact id
- use both full-doc and passage-split pipelines (keep candidate order deterministic)
- try pad-mode single and bucketed 512/1024
- run with and without our small prefix prompt (we prime with "Answer concisely:")
- log top-5 candidate id lists for failure cases

maya: starting with tokenizer + normalization parity. will post results. if ndcg gap persists we can run a calibration PTQ that preserves range for LN layers (per PTQ docs).
sam: fyi, when we saw an ndcg bump previously it correlated with stable candidate sampling (same tie-break ordering) — add a checksum of candidate order to the eval metadata so we can diff runs easily.
maya: added `--candidate-checksum` to the command and re-ran. results coming in (will post short table).
alex: if this is reproducing only on full-doc, we might need to split candidates into passages for the quantized variant as a stop-gap. not ideal but practical.
maya: re-run finished: fp16 ndcg@10=0.412, int8=0.400 (with normalization + same tokenizer), padding=bucket512 -> int8=0.405. so bucketed padding recovered ~0.5% ndcg.
li: nice — suggests the discrepancy is sequence-length / kernel scheduling related. caching/batch packing differences during autoreg generation can change ranker scores slightly.
sam: can you paste an example failing query + top-5 ids? I'll check tie-breaks.
maya: pasted sample below:
```
query: "how to rotate logs in nginx?"
fp16 top5: [doc_342, doc_19, doc_88, doc_411, doc_7]
int8 top5: [doc_19, doc_342, doc_88, doc_411, doc_7]
```
maya: same scores but different tie-break order for first two -> ndcg swing.
alex: that matches tie-breaker hypothesis. score equalities + nondeterministic ordering in our sort implementation caused the swap. int8 probe likely changed floating rounding so tiny diffs push equal scores across threshold.
li: next actions: make deterministic stable sort by (score, doc_id) in eval harness, re-eval. also add tie-breaker test in CI for quant bring-ups.
maya: filing a quick PR to stable-sort and to add bucket512 as default for ranker onboarding tests. assigning to @li for CI test and @alex for tokenizer artifact pin. I will re-run final baseline after CI changes. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: PR #1284 created by maya: https://git.internal/pull/1284 (title: "stable sort + onboarding bucketed padding")
maya: thanks all — will update thread when CI finishes and when final numbers are stable. :eyes:
